concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Prarthana Samaj was established at Bombay in the year __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1867**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 by **Atmaram Pandurang** in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The Samaj aimed to make social reforms in Hindu society by introducing **rational and humanistic principles**.
 
• It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and worked towards **abolishing caste discrimination** and promoting women's education.
 
• Notable figures like **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade** and **R. G. Bhandarkar** were actively involved in the Samaj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj**

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it was one of the earliest socio-religious reform movements in India.
 
• It aimed to reform Hindu society by **abolishing practices like Sati** and promoting monotheism.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj emphasized **rationalism and humanism** in religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade**
 
 
• An Indian scholar, social reformer, and one of the founding members of the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• He was a strong advocate for **women's education and widow remarriage**.
 
• Ranade also played a significant role in the formation of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
 
 
• **R. G. Bhandarkar**
 
 
• An Indian scholar, orientalist, and social reformer who significantly contributed to the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• He is known for his work in the **field of Indian history and culture**.
 
• Bhandarkar was also a **pioneer in the field of Sanskrit studies**.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms in 19th Century India**
 
 
• The 19th century witnessed a wave of socio-religious reform movements aimed at **eliminating social evils** and promoting progressive ideas.
 
• These reforms were spearheaded by various organizations and individuals who emphasized **education, women's rights, and caste equality**.
 
• The reform movements played a crucial role in **modernizing Indian society** and laying the foundation for the Indian independence movement.
